message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo was one of the bloodiest engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  While estimates vary depending on how “casualties” are counted (killed, wounded, missing, or captured), most historians agree that roughly **45 000–50 000 soldiers** lost their lives, were wounded, or went missing across both sides.  

A commonly cited breakdown is:

| Side | Killed | Wounded | Missing/Captured | Total |
|------|--------|---------|------------------|-------|
| French & allies | ~12 000 | ~13 000 | ~10 000 | ~35 000 |
| Anglo‑Dutch & Prussian coalition | ~8 000 | ~9 000 | ~5 000 | ~22 000 |

Adding the two totals gives an overall casualty count of about **57 000** when you include all categories.  If you restrict yourself to those who died or were wounded, the figure drops to roughly **45 000**.  

So, while the precise number depends on the source and definition used, it’s safe to say that somewhere between **45 000 and 60 000** soldiers suffered casualties at Waterloo.
